KEMUDAHAN-KEMUDAHAN PERUBATAN :
(Z)

Kemudahan-kemudahan seseorang Hakim
dan ahli keluarganya

Rawatan perubatan percuma bagi Hakim, isteri-isteri
dan anak-anak mereka tetapi, jika dimasukkan ke
hospital, Hakim itu hendaklah membayar caj harian
wad atas kadar $8 seorang. Seseorang Hakim adalah
berhak menerima dengan percuma apa-apa ubat,
bantuan dan rawatan perubatan sebagaimana yang
dapat diadakan oleh Kerajaan, termasuklah anggota
badan tiruan dan alat-alat orthopaedik.

(D
Jenis cuti dan bilangan hari yang layak
bagi seseorang Hakim
(a) Cuti Rehat

Mengikut kadar 35 hari dalam satu tahun tidak
termasuk hari kelepasan am dan hari kelepasan
mingguan. Cuti rehat hendaklah diambil dalam
tahun cuti itu terakru dan jika disebabkan oleh
kepentingan perkhidmatan, cuti tidak diambil
dalam tahun itu, maka cuti itu bolehlah dibawa
ke hadapan dalam tahun berikutnya. Cuti rehat
bagi mana-mana tiga tahun berturut-turut boleh
dikumpulkan bagi maksud perjalanan keluar
negeri dan pengumpulan cuti dan perjalanan ke-
luar negeri itu adalah tertakluk kepada kelulusan
terlebih dahulu. Pihakberkuasa yang meluluskan
bagi maksud perenggan ini ialah—

(i) bagi Ketua Hakim Negara, Perdana Menteri;

(ii) bagi Hakim Besar dan Hakim-hakim Per-
sekutuan, Ketua Hakim Negara;

(iii) bagi Hakim-hakim lain, Hakim Besar yang
berkenaan.

(b) Cuti Sakit

Cuti sakit hingga 90 hari pada satu masa atau
hingga maksimum 90 hari dalam sesuatu tahun
(Januari hingga Disember). Tetapi cuti sakit tam-
bahan tidak lebih daripada 90 hari boleh diberi
dengan kelulusan Perdana Menteri bagi Ketua
Hakim Negara dan dengan kelulusan Ketua
Hakim Negara bagi Hakim-hakim lain.

(c) Cuti Tibi
Hingga maksimum 12 bulan bergaji penuh.

Kemudian daripada itu, 6 bulan bergaji separuh
dan 6 bulan lagi tanpa gaji.

JUDGES' REMUNERATION ACT 1971

JUDGES' REMUNBRATION (AMENDMENT OF SECOND SCHEDULB)
REGULATIONS 1979

In exercise of the powers conferred by section 19 of the Judges'
Remuneration Act 1971, the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, after consultation
with the Lord President, makes the following regulations:

1. These Regulations may be cited as the Judges' Remuneration
(Amendment of Second Schedule) Regulations 1979 and shall, in
accordance with the provisions of the Judges' Remuneration (Amend-
ment) Act 1979, apply to the Judges to whom that Act applies.

2. The Judges' Remuneration Act 1971 is amended by substituting for
the Second Schedule the following new Second Schedule—

(J)

Allowance for a Judge

A Judge shall be eligible to an allowance of $500
payable once in 10 years.

MEDICAL FACILITIES:

(D
Facilities of a Judge and
members of his family

Free medical treatment for Judges, their wives and
children but, in case of hospitalisation, the Judge
shall pay ward daily charges at the rate of $8 per
person. A Judge shall be entitled to receive free of
charge such medicines, medical assistance and
attendance as Government has at its disposal,
including artificial limbs and orthopaedic appliances.

LEAVE:
(D)
Type of leave and number of days
to which a Judge is entitled

(a) Vacation Leave

At the rate of 35 days in a year excluding public
holidays and weekly holidays. Vacation leave
shall be taken in the year in which it accrues ahd
where, owing to exigencies of service, it has not
been taken in such year, it can be carried forward
into the succeeding year. Vacation leave in
respect of any three consecutive years may be
accumulated for the purpose of overseas travel
and such accumulation and overseas travel shall
be subject to prior approval. The approving
authority for the purpose of this paragraph shall
be—
(i) in the case of the Lord President, the Prime
Minister;
(ii) in the case of the Chief Justices and the
Federal Judges, the Lord President;
(iii) in the case of other Judges, the Chief
Justice concerned.

(b) Medical Leave

Sick leave up to 90 days at one time or up to a
maximum of 90 days in any one year (January
to December). But additional medical leave of not
more than 90 days may be given with the
approval of the Prime Minister in the case of the
Lord President and of the Lord President in the
case of other Judges.

(c) Tuberculosis Leave

Up to a maximum of 12 months on full pay.
Thereafter, 6 months on half-pay and further 6
months without pay.

13. DEATH AND INJURY BENEFITS IN AIRCRAFT ACCIDENTS:

(D)                                                     (2)
Benefits to a Judge or
his dependants                                     Effective Date

Liabilities for an injury or death arising out of an 3-9-1971
aircraft accident in the course of duty shall be borne

entirely by the Government. The rates of death and
disablement benefits for Judges arising from such

accidents shall be as follows—

(a) For death caused by an injury sustained in an
accident, a sum of $150,000:

Provided that where the dependants or legal
personal representatives are entitled to receive
similar benefits under any other provisions of
this Act, such dependants or legal personal
representatives shall be entitled at their option
to receive one benefit only.

(b) For permanent disablement caused by an injury
sustained in an accident resulting in—

(i) loss of two or more limbs by actual
separation at or above the wrist or ankle;
or the total and irrecoverable loss of all
sight of both eyes; or the loss of one limb
accompanied by the loss of sight of one
eye: $275,000;

(ii) loss of one limb by actual separation at
or above the wrist or ankle; or the total
and irrecoverable loss of sight of one
eye: $150,000;

(iii) total incapacity (total disablement) from
engaging in or giving attention to any
profession or occupation: $275,000;

(iv) partial disablement: proportionate, ac-
cording to medical assessment of the
percentage degree of such disablement.
